task: Fix the authentication bypass introduced by the middleware refactor.

candidate_memories.content: Integration tests show that requests with an expired token now bypass the authentication middleware.
Authentication middleware must be registered before the route handlers in the middleware chain.
The middleware refactor moved authentication to a sub-router but forgot to apply it to the root router.
When refactoring middleware chains, audit the full route registration order before and after the change.
The bypass only affects requests to the root router paths; sub-router paths still authenticate correctly.
The API gateway is configured to forward the Authorization header to the upstream service.
Session 5 note: a new API key authentication method was added alongside JWT.
Old practice: authentication was enforced at the route level with decorators before middleware was adopted.
The session management library was upgraded in the last sprint to support refresh tokens.
Security scan in session 14 found no other authentication bypass issues in the sub-router paths.
Old middleware guide: the authentication middleware ran after the logging middleware in the old chain.
Middleware registration order determines execution order; authentication must precede all business logic.
Session 9 note: the API documentation was updated to reflect the new authentication endpoints.
The OAuth integration uses a third-party authorization server with a 24-hour token lifetime.
Session 7 note: rate limiting was moved from the application to the API gateway.
Two-factor authentication is implemented as a separate middleware that runs after basic auth.
After any middleware refactor, run a full authentication matrix test covering all route prefixes.
Session 11 note: the login failure audit log was extended to include IP addresses.
Old auth guide: routes under /api/v1/public were intentionally excluded from authentication.
JWT tokens are validated using RS256 with the public key fetched from the JWKS endpoint.
